summary:
Turn 79 closed the delay-table unread item as a bounded negative result and named the single premise a future change would break.

What was understood. When a latency table is configured, client proposals pass through a per-connection ordering structure that releases a proposal to the replica's propose channel only when it continues a contiguous run from command-id zero: the traversal starts from -1 and handles a node only when the last handled id equals the node's id minus one. A connection whose first proposal carries any other command id would therefore never be delivered — the proposal sits in the structure and the client waits forever — while the delay arithmetic itself is a per-direction half of the configured value.

Why the premise holds here. The captured client numbers its proposals from zero (seqnum initialised to -1 and incremented before use) and creates one connection per run, and although a Reconnect method exists in the client library it has no call site anywhere in the repository, so no connection is ever reused with a continuing command-id sequence. The mechanism that would block a client is therefore present but unreachable in this snapshot — a bounded negative result rather than a defect, with the exact premise recorded so a future reconnect or a second connection per client clone is recognised as the trigger.

Product. Three new sources register the helper's ordering range and the two client facts; the feedback records the answer, the residual (whether a deployment ever passes `-latency`, and what a future reconnecting caller would do), and keeps the reader-side codec consequence and the two paused candidates visible. Audit spec moved to version 17; the eleven claim families and every reviewed result are untouched, and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
